Subject: Intermittent stalls during streaming completions

Hi Aditya,

We're seeing intermittent stalls in streaming responses from the Redwood API over the last 48 hours. The client-side library shows an open websocket/stream but no tokens arrive for ~20–40s, after which the stream either resumes or closes with a 502. This is impacting our live UX for payment confirmation.

We've attached a short log excerpt (orion_logs_20260918.txt) showing one occurrence; timestamps are in UTC. The pattern seems to occur primarily on longer generated replies (>= 400 tokens) but not exclusively. Can someone from your side confirm whether there were capacity issues or infra events in us-west during that window?

Thanks,
Rohan Patel

Hi Rohan — I'm Marissa from Support, picking this up. I ran a repro against the timestamps you sent using the same model family and a similar prompt shape. Quick summary of what I attempted:

- Replayed request payloads with streaming enabled and long max_tokens (500+).
- Simulated sustained token production and artificially injected client-side pauses.
- Pulled server-side traces for the window 2026-09-17T22:30:00Z–2026-09-18T02:15:00Z.

Findings so far:
- Platform traces show normal request handling with no GPU allocation errors and no runtime OOMs.
- We saw a couple of short-lived proxy connection resets (2–3s) in the edge logs in us-west-2 during that period; they did not line up exactly with the timestamps in your log snippet.
- No token-generation stalls appear in the server-side transcript for the exact request ids we could correlate; the backend emitted tokens continuously until the client-side stream closed in all correlated cases.

I'm attaching the platform trace we pulled (platform_trace_20260919.json) and a short excerpt of the reconstructed server transcript. Can you confirm whether you see a corresponding disconnect on your side at the same UTC timestamp, or whether your client reports any network-level timeouts?

If we can't correlate the next step would be to run a live repro with your team connected so we can capture packet-level traces and SDK logs simultaneously.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls during streaming completions — Investigation result and recommended next steps

Hi Luis / Rohan — follow-up after a full investigation:

Summary:
- We reviewed server-side traces, instance logs, and network proxies for the windows you reported (9/17–9/19). No evidence of model runtime stalls, OOMs, or long tail CPU/GPU queuing that would cause 20–40s token pauses.
- Edge logs show a small number of connection resets in us-west-2 unrelated to token generation; these are transient (seconds) and were not coupled to backend delays in our correlated samples.
- The HAR and console logs you provided (thank you) show the client-side websocket being backgrounded by the browser's service worker when the tab is not active — the app's JS runtime suspends the event loop and pauses processing of the incoming stream for ~25–35s in those cases.

Conclusion:
- Based on available evidence, the root cause appears to be client-side suspension (service-worker/tab backgrounding) causing perceived stalls, not a server-side token-generation stall. We could not reproduce a server-driven 20–40s stall in any correlated request id.

Actions taken and recommendations:
- Filing: created internal trace link: https://redwood-internal/trace/trace-98173 for engineering audit.
- Suggested mitigations for Orion Pay: implement a small client-side buffer to surface partial tokens immediately, add a short heartbeat/ping to detect backgrounding, and consider switching to a background-friendly delivery method (long polling fallback) for critical UI flows.
- If you'd prefer, we can run a dedicated live debug session during your peak window to capture packet-level traces; this will let us rule out intermittent network appliances between your users and the edge.

I'll leave this ticket in a "monitor" state; if you see another occurrence after applying the client mitigations please reopen and we'll escalate. Thanks for working with us on the data — that made correlation straightforward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
